questions.question: The principal nitrogenous waste products excreted by human kidneys are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urea and uric acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human body generates nitrogenous waste primarily from the metabolism of **proteins** and **nucleic acids**.
 
• **Ammonia** is the immediate byproduct of protein deamination, which is highly toxic; the **liver** converts it into **urea** through the **Ornithine cycle** (also known as the **Urea cycle**) to facilitate safe transport in the blood.
 
• **Urea** constitutes the largest portion of nitrogenous waste in human urine, and humans are therefore classified as **ureotelic** organisms.
 
• **Uric acid** is a nitrogenous byproduct formed during the catabolism of **purines**, which are essential components of nucleotides like **adenine** and **guanine** found in DNA and RNA.
 
• The **kidneys** serve as the primary organ for **osmoregulation** and excretion, where **nephrons** perform **ultrafiltration** to separate these nitrogenous wastes from the bloodstream for elimination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon dioxide and oxygen**:

 
 
• **Carbon dioxide** is a byproduct of **cellular respiration** but is primarily excreted via the **lungs** through expiration.
 
• **Oxygen** is an essential gas required for **aerobic respiration** and is not a waste product.
 
 
 
• **Amino acids and glucose**:
 
 
• These are vital nutrients; in healthy individuals, the **Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)** of the kidney reabsorbs nearly 100% of **glucose** and **amino acids** back into the blood.
 
 
 
• **Fatty acids and glycerol**:
 
 
• These are products of **lipid digestion** and are used for **energy production** or stored in **adipose tissues** rather than being excreted as nitrogenous wastes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common example of non-biodegradable waste?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plastic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Non-biodegradable waste** is defined as any **pollutant** or material that cannot be broken down, decomposed, or dissolved by **natural agents** such as **bacteria**, **fungi**, and other **microorganisms**.
 
• **Plastic** is a common example of this category because it is a **synthetic polymer** primarily derived from **petrochemicals**

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of reducing in waste management?

options.text: Using a paint bucket multiple times
Switching from plastic bags to jute bags
Throwing aluminium cans in the trash

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Switching from plastic bags to jute bags**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reduce** is the most prioritized component of the **waste management hierarchy** (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle), focusing on **waste prevention** by minimizing the amount of material used at the source.
 
• Switching from plastic bags to **jute bags** is a primary example of reduction because it eliminates the need for multiple **single-use plastic bags** that would otherwise end up in **landfills** or oceans.
 
• **Plastics** are derived from **petroleum products** and are **non-biodegradable**, often persisting in the environment for hundreds of years, whereas **jute** is a **natural fiber** that is **biodegradable** and **sustainable**.
 
• By choosing a long-lasting, **reusable jute bag**, a consumer effectively **reduces** the demand for plastic production and the subsequent generation of plastic waste, addressing the problem of **environmental pollution** at its origin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reuse**:

 
 
• Using a **paint bucket multiple times** is classified as **reusing** because the item is utilized repeatedly for the same or a new purpose without being processed into a new raw material.
 
 
 
• **Recycle**:
 
 
• **Recycling old newspapers** involves collecting waste paper and processing it back into **pulp** to manufacture new paper products, which helps in saving **trees** and **energy** compared to virgin production.
 
 
 
• **Waste Disposal**:
 
 
• Throwing items like **aluminium cans** in the trash is not a management strategy but a form of **disposal**; however, aluminium is 100% **recyclable** and should ideally be diverted from the waste stream.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**:
 
 
• Effective **source reduction** conserves **natural resources**, reduces **greenhouse gas emissions**, and saves **energy** required for the extraction and manufacturing of new products.

questions.question: Which architectural element is used in Rajput cenotaphs and memorials?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhatri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhatris** are elevated, dome-shaped pavilions that serve as **cenotaphs** or memorials in Indian architecture, particularly prominent in **Rajput** and **Maratha** styles.
 
• The term is derived from the Sanskrit word for **umbrella**, symbolizing protection, pride, and honor bestowed upon the deceased.
 
• These structures are typically built at the **cremation sites** of royalty and noblemen, serving as a lasting tribute rather than a tomb, as **Hinduism** generally practices cremation.
 
• Architecturally, they consist of a **raised plinth** (Jagati) supporting several **pillars**, which in turn support a central dome or multiple smaller domes often decorated with **inverted lotus** motifs.
 
• Famous examples in **Rajasthan** include the **Royal Gaitor** in Jaipur, the **Ahar Cenotaphs** in Udaipur, and the **Bada Bagh** in Jaisalmer, showcasing intricate **sandstone** and **marble** carvings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Garbhagriha**:

 
 
• Refers to the **sanctum sanctorum** or the innermost chamber of a Hindu temple.
 
• It houses the **primary deity** and is usually a small, unadorned square room designed for focused worship.
 
 
 
• **Stepwell**:
 
 
• Locally known as **Baori**, **Bawdi**, or **Vav**, these are deep wells with a flight of steps leading to the water level.
 
• They were essential for **water management** and social gatherings in the arid regions of **Western India**.
 
 
 
• **Gopuram**:
 
 
• A monumental, ornate **entrance tower** characteristic of **Dravidian architecture**.
 
• These are found predominantly in **South Indian** temple complexes, often towering over the main shrine.

questions.question: On the basis of function, which of the following is not a type of animal tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vascular tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Epithelial tissue** consists of cells that form a continuous sheet to cover the external body surfaces and line the internal organs and cavities for protection and secretion. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Connective tissue** is responsible for binding, supporting, and packing various organs of the body, and it includes specialized forms like **bone**, **cartilage**, and **blood**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Muscular tissue** is made up of elongated cells called **muscle fibers** that contain contractile proteins, enabling the body to perform movement and locomotion. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Vascular tissue** is a specialized conducting tissue found in **plants**, consisting of **Xylem** and **Phloem**, which facilitate the transport of water and nutrients. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• In animals, the components of the **circulatory system** (veins, arteries, and blood) are classified under **epithelial** and **connective tissues** rather than being labeled as a separate 'vascular tissue' category in histology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Animal Tissues**:

 
 
• **Nervous Tissue**: Composed of **neurons** that receive and transmit electrochemical impulses, primarily located in the **brain** and **spinal cord**.
 
• **Muscular Tissue Subtypes**: Includes **Skeletal** (striated/voluntary), **Smooth** (non-striated/involuntary), and **Cardiac** (heart muscles).
 
• **Epithelial Subtypes**: Categorized as **Squamous**, **Cuboidal**, or **Columnar** based on cell shape.
 
 
 
• **Plant Vascular System**:
 
 
• **Xylem**: Responsible for the unidirectional transport of **water** and **dissolved minerals** from roots to leaves.
 
• **Phloem**: Responsible for the bidirectional transport of **organic nutrients** (food) from leaves to other storage organs.

questions.question: Animals living in water and on land are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amphibians**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Amphibians** are a class of **ectothermic** (cold-blooded) vertebrate animals that belong to the group **Lissamphibia**. They are unique for their **dual life cycle**, which allows them to inhabit both **aquatic** and **terrestrial** environments.
 
• The term is derived from the Greek words **amphi**, meaning 'both', and **bios**, meaning 'life', highligh

questions.concept: Ecology and Functions of an ecosystem
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about decomposers?

options.text: They recycle nutrients back into the soil

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They recycle nutrients back into the soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Decomposers** are organisms, primarily **bacteria** and **fungi**, that break down dead or decaying organic matter, including animal remains and leaf litter.
 
• The biological process of **decomposition** involves the conversion of complex organic substances into simpler **inorganic matter** such as carbon dioxide, water, and nutrients.
 
• By breaking down the **detritus**, these organisms release essential chemical elements like **nitrogen**, **phosphorus**, and **potassium** back into the ecosystem.
 
• These recycled nutrients are absorbed by the **soil**, where they become available for uptake by **primary producers** (plants) to sustain new growth.
 
• This function is critical for maintaining **ecological balance** and completing the **nutrient cycle**, ensuring that life-sustaining minerals are not permanently lost to the environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Autotrophic Organisms**:

 
 
• These are **producers**, such as green plants and algae, that synthesize their own food using **sunlight** (photosynthesis) or chemical energy (chemosynthesis).
 
• **Decomposers** are actually **heterotrophic**, specifically **saprotrophs**, because they rely on external organic sources for energy.
 
 
 
• **Consumers and Predators**:
 
 
• Organisms that **eat live animals** are known as **carnivores** or predators, occupying higher **trophic levels** in the food web.
 
• **Scavengers** like vultures initiate the breakdown of large carcasses, but only **decomposers** finish the process at a molecular level.
 
 
 
• **Plant Nutrition**:
 
 
• While decomposers provide the **raw inorganic minerals**, plants produce their own 'food' (glucose) via the **chloroplasts** in their leaves.

questions.question: Which Odisha-based politician exited active politics in June 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**V. K. Pandian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **V. K. Pandian**, a former bureaucrat turned politician, announced his withdrawal from active politics on **June 9, 2024**.
 
• This decision followed the **Biju Janata Dal (BJD)** party's defeat in the **2024 Odisha Legislative Assembly** and **Lok Sabha** elections, which ended the 24-year governance of **Naveen Patnaik**.
 
• He is a former **IAS officer** of the **2000 batch** who served as the **Private Secretary** to Chief Minister **Naveen Patnaik** for over a decade before taking voluntary retirement in **October 2023**.
 
• After retiring from the civil services, he was appointed as the **Chairman of 5T** (Transparency, Technology, Teamwork, Time, and Transformation) and **Nabin Odisha** with a cabinet rank.
 
• Pandian formally joined the **Biju Janata Dal** in **November 2023** and played a central role in the party's 2024 election campaign strategy.
 
• In his exit statement, he clarified that his entry into politics was solely to assist his mentor, **Naveen Patnaik**, and expressed regret if his presence was used as a tool by political opponents to target the party.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Naveen Patnaik**:

 
 
• The founder-president of the **Biju Janata Dal** and the longest-serving Chief Minister of **Odisha** (2000−2024).
 
• Following the 2024 electoral defeat, he took over the role of the **Leader of Opposition** in the Odisha Assembly.
 
 
 
• **Baijayant Panda**:
 
 
• A senior leader and National Vice President of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**.
 
• He successfully contested and won the **Kendrapara** Lok Sabha seat in the 2024 general elections.
 
 
 
• **Dharmendra Pradhan**:
 
 
• A prominent **BJP** leader and the current **Union Minister of Education** in the Government of India.
 
• He won the **Sambalpur** Lok Sabha seat in 2024, marking his return to direct electoral politics after several years in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: In August 2024 who has been appointed as Director General of the Border Security Force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Daljit Singh Chaudhary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Daljit Singh Chaudhary**, a distinguished **1990-batch Indian Police Service (IPS)** officer of the **Uttar Pradesh cadre**, was appointed as the **Director General (DG)** of the **Border Security Force (BSF)** in **August 2024**.
 
• The **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)** approved his appointment for a term ending on **November 30, 2025**, coinciding with his date of superannuation.
 
• Prior to this role, he was serving as the **Director General** of the **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)** and was also holding the additional charge of the **National Security Guard (NSG)**.
 
• He took over the command from **Nitin Agarwal**, who was prematurely repatriated to his state cadre by the Union Government.
 
• This appointment is critical as the **BSF** is responsible for the internal security and border integrity of India, especially along the **Pakistan** and **Bangladesh** frontiers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Border Security Force (BSF)**:

 
 
• Established on **December 1, 1965**, it is one of the seven **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF)** of India.
 
• It functions under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Home Affairs** and is headquartered in **New Delhi**.
 
• The primary mandate of the **BSF** is to ensure the security of the borders of India and matters connected therewith; it is often called the **First Line of Defence**.
 
• The motto of the force is **Jeevan Paryant Kartavya** (Duty Unto Death).
 
 
 
• **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)**:
 
 
• Another **CAPF** established in **1963**, primarily tasked with guarding India's borders with **Nepal** and **Bhutan**.

questions.question: What is the primary function of villi in the small intestine in humans?

options.text: To increase the surface area for absorption

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To increase the surface area for absorption**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Villi** are tiny, finger-like projections that line the inner walls of the **small intestine** in the human digestive system.
 
• The primary function of these structures is to dramatically increase the **surface area** available for the absorption of digested food molecules into the bloodstream.
 
• Increased surface area is critical because the rate of **nutrient absorption** is directly proportional to the surface area in contact with the **chyme** (partially digested food).
 
• Each villus contains a network of **blood capillaries** and a central lymphatic vessel known as a **lacteal**, which facilitate the immediate transport of nutrients.
 
• Without villi, the small intestine would need to be considerably longer to absorb the same amount of **glucose**, **amino acids**, and **fatty acids** required by the body.
 
• The epithelial cells covering the villi further possess **microvilli**, which together create a **brush border**, increasing the absorptive surface area by nearly 600 times compared to a flat surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lacteals**:

 
 
• These are specialized **lymphatic capillaries** located inside each villus.
 
• They are responsible for absorbing **dietary fats** and fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K) that are too large to enter blood capillaries directly.
 
 
 
• **Digestive Enzymes**:
 
 
• While the **pancreas** and **stomach** secrete major enzymes, the **brush border** of the villi also produces enzymes like **maltase**, **sucrase**, and **lactase** to finalize the digestion of carbohydrates.
 
 
 
• **Neutralizing Stomach Acid**:
 
 
• This process is primarily handled by **bicarbonate ions** released from the **pancreas** into the **duodenum**, rather than by the villi themselves.
 
 
 
• **Food Breakdown**:
 
 
• Mechanical breakdown occurs through **mastication** in the mouth and **peristalsis** in the stomach; villi only handle the end-stage absorption of the broken-down molecules.

questions.question: The Aravalli Green wall Project does NOT cover which of the following state?
questions.solution:
**Key Points**

 
• The **Aravalli Green Wall Project** is a major environmental initiative launched by the **Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** in March 2023.
 
• The project is designed to combat **desertification** and **land degradation** by creating a **5 km wide green belt** buffer around the **Aravalli Mountain Range**.
 
• This initiative aligns with Indias goal to restore **26 million hectares** of degraded land by 2030, supporting the **United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD)**.
 
• The primary objective is to act as a barrier against the eastward expansion of the **Thar Desert** and to improve the **ecological health** of the region.

**Additional Information**

 
• The **Aravalli Mountain Range** naturally stretches across four regions in North and West India.
 
• The project specifically covers the states and Union Territories where these hills are located: **Gujarat**, **Rajasthan**, **Haryana**, and **Delhi**.
 
• Key activities under this project include **afforestation**, **reforestation**, and the **restoration of local water bodies** (rejuvenation of ponds and lakes).
 
• While **Haryana**, **Rajasthan**, and **Gujarat** are integral parts of the project area, **Maharashtra** is situated further south and is not part of the **Aravalli geographical corridor**.

**Conclusion**

The **Aravalli Green Wall Project** includes Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, and Delhi. It does not include **Maharashtra**. **Therefore, the correct answer is Maharashtra.**

questions.question: The SLV-3 rocket used for India's first satellite launch was a ____ stage rocket.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Satellite Launch Vehicle-3 (SLV-3)** was **India's** first experimental satellite launch vehicle, developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• The **SLV-3** was designed as a **four-stage** rocket, where every stage utilized **solid propellant motors** to achieve the necessary velocity for orbital injection.
 
• The project was spearheaded by the eminent scientist **Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**, who served as the **Project Director**, leading a team of hundreds of engineers and scientists.
 
• On **July 18, 1980**, the vehicle was successfully launched from the **Sriharikota Range (SHAR)**, now known as the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre**.
 
• The primary mission of the **SLV-3** was to place the **40 kg** **Rohini satellite (RS-1)** into a **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**, a feat that made **India** the sixth nation to join the exclusive club of space-faring countries.
 
• The **four-stage** configuration allowed the rocket to shed mass progressively, ensuring the final stage could reach the speed of approximately **28,000 km/h** required for orbit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Technical Specifications of the SLV-3**:

 
 
• The vehicle stood at a total height of **22.7 meters** and possessed a lift-off mass of **17 tonnes**.
 
• All four stages used **Hydroxyl Terminated Polybutadiene (HTPB)** based solid propellants, which were chosen for their reliability and ease of storage.
 
• The **first stage** (S1) was the largest, generating a maximum thrust of **43 tonnes** to lift the vehicle off the launch pad.
 
 
 
• **Legacy and Successor Vehicles**:
 
 
• The technological breakthroughs achieved with the **four-stage** **SLV-3** served as the foundation for the **Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle (ASLV)**.
 
• It eventually led to the development of the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)**, which incorporates both **solid and liquid propulsion** stages and has become **ISRO's** most reliable workhorse.
 
• The success of **SLV-3** validated **India's** capability in **multistage propulsion**, **inertial navigation**, and **real-time tracking** systems.

questions.question: In Chhattisgarh, which folk songs are sung with the onset of the spring season?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Faag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Faag** is a traditional folk song genre of **Chhattisgarh**, predominantly sung to welcome the **Spring season** (Vasant Ritu).
 
• These songs are performed during the Hindu month of **Phalguna**, which typically falls between **February and March**, marking the transition from winter.
 
• The performance of Faag is inseparable from the **Holi** festival celebrations, serving as a medium to express the joy of the 'Festival of Colors'.
 
• In rural and tribal communities of **Chhattisgarh**, Faag is a communal activity where singers gather in groups to perform rhythmic and energetic compositions.
 
• The musical accompaniment usually features traditional instruments like the **Nagara** (kettledrum), **Dholak**, and **Manjira**, which provide the upbeat tempo essential to the genre.
 
• The lyrical content often highlights the blooming of **Palash** and **Semal** flowers, agricultural prosperity, and the divine play of **Radha and Krishna**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rai**:

 
 
• This is a famous folk dance and music tradition of the **Bundelkhand** region in **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It is traditionally performed by the **Bedia** tribe to celebrate weddings, births, and the successful completion of a harvest.
 
 
 
• **Kolatam**:
 
 
• A traditional stick dance originating from **Andhra Pradesh** and practiced across **South India**.
 
• It involves performers moving in a circle and striking wooden sticks in a synchronized rhythmic pattern, similar to the **Dandiya Raas**.
 
 
 
• **Kawini**:
 
 
• While **Chhattisgarh** has diverse folk music forms like **Pandwani**, **Panthi**, and **Soowa**, **Kawini** is not recognized as a primary spring-related folk song of the state.

questions.question: 'Gajan' folk songs, depicting a dialogue between gods, are traditionally associated with which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gajan** is a traditional folk festival celebrated with great fervor in **West Bengal**, primarily during the month of **Chaitra** (March-April), coinciding with the **Bengali New Year**.
 
• The **Gajan folk songs** are an integral part of this ritualistic festival, which is dedicated to the worship of deities like **Lord Shiva**, **Dharmathakur**, and **Nil**.
 
• The theme of these songs often revolves around a **dialogue between gods**, particularly Lord Shiva and Parvati, reflecting the agricultural and domestic concerns of the rural population.
 
• Devotees, known as **Sannyasis** or **Bhaktas**, perform these songs while dressed as various deities or mythological characters, accompanied by traditional instruments like the **Dhak** and **Kansar**.
 
• The festival serves as a platform for **social equality**, where people from various castes participate together in the rituals and singing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Etymology and Forms**:

 
 
• The term **Gajan** is believed to be derived from the word **Garjan**, which means roar, representing the collective chanting of the devotees.
 
• In the **Malda** district of West Bengal, a similar folk form called **Gambhira** is performed, which also includes a dialogue-based interaction with the deity **Shiva**.
 
 
 
• **Other Regional Folk Forms**:
 
 
• **Maharashtra** is known for its high-energy folk forms like **Lavani** and **Powada**, which focus on storytelling and valor.
 
• **Punjab** is famous for **Bhangra** and **Gidda**, which are celebratory harvest dances, while **Nagaland** is known for tribal folk songs like **Heliamlo**.

questions.question: "Payyoli Express" is nickname related to which of the following sportsperson?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PT Usha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PT Usha**, born **Pilavullakandi Thekkeparambil Usha**, is a legendary Indian track and field athlete often hailed as the **Queen of Indian Track and Field**.
 
• The nickname **Payyoli Express** originates from her hometown, **Payyoli**, situated in the **Kozhikode district** of **Kerala**.
 
• She gained global recognition during the **1984 Los Angeles Olympics**, where she competed in the **400m hurdles** and finished fourth, missing the bronze medal by a heartbreaking margin of **0.01 seconds**.
 
• Her career reached its pinnacle at the **1986 Seoul Asian Games**, where she won **four gold medals** and one silver medal, setting multiple games records.
 
• She was awarded the **Padma Shri** and the **Arjuna Award** in **1985** for her stellar achievements in athletics and currently serves as the **President** of the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milkha Singh**:

 
 
• Widely known as **The Flying Sikh**, he was a track and field sprinter who won gold at the **1958 Commonwealth Games** and multiple **Asian Games** golds.
 
 
 
• **Dutee Chand**:
 
 
• A professional sprinter and national record holder in the women's **100m event**, she is often nicknamed the **Chand Express**.
 
 
 
• **Roshan Mistry**:
 
 
• She was a pioneering female athlete who became the first Indian woman to win a medal at the **Asian Games**, securing silver in the **100m sprint** at the **1951 New Delhi Games**.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Nicknames**:
 
 
• **Hima Das**: Known as the **Dhing Express**, representing the state of **Assam**.
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand**: Known as **The Wizard** of Hockey due to his extraordinary ball control.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a side effect of Narcotics in sports?

I. Narcotics decrease heart rate.

II. It causes vomiting.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narcotics**, specifically **opioid analgesics** such as **morphine**, **methadone**, and **pethidine**, act directly on the **central nervous system** to alleviate intense pain. A significant physiological side effect of these substances is the depression of the **autonomic nervous system**, which leads to **bradycardia** (a notable **decrease in heart rate**) and reduced **blood pressure**. **Hence, statement I is correct.**
 
• The ingestion of narcotics frequently stimulates the **chemoreceptor trigger zone** located in the **medulla oblongata** of the brain. This stimulation, combined with the irritation of the **gastrointestinal tract**, commonly results in symptoms of **nausea** and **vomiting**. These reactions are among the most prevalent acute adverse effects reported by individuals using these substances. **Hence, statement II is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narcotics** are strictly monitored and banned in-competition by the **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)** because they allow athletes to perform beyond their natural pain threshold, risking severe injury.

 
 
• **Respiratory Depression**: The most severe risk involves a decrease in the **respiratory drive**, which can lead to inadequate **oxygenation** of the blood and potentially fatal outcomes.
 
• **Impaired Coordination**: These substances cause **drowsiness**, loss of **mental focus**, and impaired **physical balance**, which can lead to accidents during athletic activities.
 
• **Addiction and Tolerance**: Long-term use often results in **physical dependence** and **addiction**, necessitating higher doses to achieve the same analgesic effect.
 
• **Gastrointestinal Issues**: Beyond vomiting, narcotics are notorious for causing chronic **constipation** by slowing down the **motility** of the digestive system.

questions.question: Status of Policing in India Report 2025 was published by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Common Cause & Lokniti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Status of Policing in India Report (SPIR)** is a comprehensive collaborative study conducted by **Common Cause** and **Lokniti**, which is a research program of the **Centre for the Study of Developing Societies (CSDS)**.
 
• The report aims to provide a data-driven assessment of the **Indian police system** by capturing the perspectives of both the **general citizenry** and the **police personnel** themselves.
 
• The **2025 edition** of the report focuses on identifying **structural gaps**, the effectiveness of **police reforms**, and the evolving relationship between the police and the public in the context of new legislative frameworks like the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita**.
 
• Unlike official government data, the **SPIR** utilizes **perception-based surveys** and **fieldwork** across multiple states to evaluate levels of **trust**, **discrimination**, and **adequacy of infrastructure** within the force.
 
• The report is widely used by **policymakers**, **academicians**, and **civil society** to advocate for **judicial** and **administrative reforms** in the security sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Cause**:

 
 
• Founded in **1980** by **H.D. Shourie**, it is a premier **non-profit organization** dedicated to championing **public interest** causes and institutional accountability in India.
 
• It has played a significant role in historical **Public Interest Litigations (PILs)** concerning **electoral reforms** and the **right to information**.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**:
 
 
• As the **National Institution for Transforming India**, it serves as the government’s apex **policy think tank**, replacing the **Planning Commission** in **2015**.
 
• It publishes significant reports like the **SDG India Index** and the **Export Preparedness Index**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)**:
 
 
• The nodal ministry responsible for **internal security** and **police administration** in India.
 
• It oversees the **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)**, which publishes the official **Crime in India** annual statistics.
 
 
 
• **DARPG**:
 
 
• The **Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances** is the nodal agency for formulating **administrative reform** policies and redressing **public grievances**.

questions.question: India Social Development Report is one of the flagship publications of _______.

options.text: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CSD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Council for Social Development (CSD)** is a premier research organization established in **1962** as a study group under the **India International Centre** and later registered as an autonomous body in **1970**.
 
• The **India Social Development Report (ISDR)** is a **flagship biennial publication** of the CSD, serving as an essential resource for academics and policymakers since its inception in **2006**.
 
• The report provides a critical analysis of India's **social sectors**, covering themes like **tribal development**, **education**, **health**, **disability**, **rural livelihoods**, and **marginalization**.
 
• **Dr. Durgabai Deshmukh**, a renowned social reformer and freedom fighter, was the **Founder President** of the CSD, emphasizing research-based advocacy for social justice and human rights.
 
• The **CSD** operates out of two main campuses located in **New Delhi** and **Hyderabad**, focusing on the **social impact** of economic policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Aayog**:

 
 
• Replaced the **Planning Commission** on **January 1, 2015**, to function as the premier policy **Think Tank** of the Government of India.
 
• It produces major indices like the **SDG India Index**, **Export Preparedness Index**, and the **Aspirational Districts Programme** reports.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**:
 
 
• Dedicated to the welfare of **Scheduled Castes**, **OBCs**, **Senior Citizens**, and **Persons with Disabilities**.
 
• It manages the **National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Autism** and various social security and pension schemes.
 
 
 
• **CPCB (Central Pollution Control Board)**:
 
 
• A **statutory organization** constituted in **1974** under the **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act**.
 
• It provides technical services to the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** regarding **air and water quality** standards and environmental regulation.

questions.question: Who is also known as 'Adi Kavi' in Indian literature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharishi Valmiki**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maharishi Valmiki** is revered as the **Adi Kavi**, which translates to the **First Poet** in the history of **Sanskrit literature**.
 
• He is the celebrated author of the **Ramayana**, one of the two great **Sanskrit epics** of **Ancient India**, containing approximately **24,000 shlokas**.
 
• The title **Adi Kavi** was given to him because he is credited with discovering the **Anustubh meter**, a rhythmic structure that transformed **Vedic Sanskrit** into **Classical Sanskrit poetry**.
 
• According to tradition, the first poetic **shloka** was born from his **shoka** (sorrow) after he witnessed a hunter killing a male **Krouncha bird** while it was with its mate.
 
• His epic work is divided into seven chapters known as **Kandas**, which trace the life, exile, and victory of **Lord Rama**, establishing the cultural and moral framework of **Dharma**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raskhan**:

 
 
• A **16th-century** poet who was born as **Syed Ibrahim Khan** but became a devout follower of **Lord Krishna**.
 
• He is famous for his **Bhakti** poetry written in the **Braj Bhasha** dialect, particularly in his works **Sujan Raskhan** and **Prem Vatika**.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya**:
 
 
• Also known as **Kautilya** or **Vishnugupta**, he was a master strategist and the prime architect of the **Mauryan Empire** under **Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• He authored the **Arthashastra**, an ancient Indian treatise on **statecraft**, **economics**, and **military strategy**.
 
 
 
• **Vishakhadatta**:
 
 
• A renowned **Sanskrit playwright** from the **Gupta period** known for his historical and political dramas.
 
• His most famous work is **Mudrarakshasa**, which details the political schemes used by **Chanakya** to secure the throne for the **Mauryan dynasty**.

questions.question: Who served as the 11th President of India from 2002 to 2007?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A. P. J. Abdul Kalam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam** served as the **11th President of India**, holding the office from **July 25, 2002, to July 25, 2007**.
 
• Widely regarded as the **Missile Man of India**, he played a critical role in the development of India's **ballistic missile** and **nuclear weapons** programs, including the **Pokhran-II** nuclear tests in 1998.
 
• Kalam was an eminent **aerospace scientist** who made significant contributions to the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** and the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**.
 
• He was popularly known as the **People's President** due to his simple lifestyle, accessibility, and his dedication to inspiring the **youth and students** of the nation.
 
• He was elected with the support of both the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** and the **Indian National Congress (INC)**, making him a rare consensus candidate for the presidency.
 
• In **1997**, he was awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian honor, becoming the third President to receive it before entering office.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pratibha Patil**:

 
 
• She served as the **12th President of India** from **2007 to 2012**.
 
• She holds the distinction of being the **first woman President** of India.
 
 
 
• **Pranab Mukherjee**:
 
 
• He served as the **13th President of India** from **2012 to 2017**.
 
• A veteran politician, he also served as the **Union Finance Minister** and was awarded the **Bharat Ratna** in 2019.
 
 
 
• **Shankar Dayal Sharma**:
 
 
• He served as the **9th President of India** from **1992 to 1997**.
 
• Prior to his presidency, he was the **8th Vice President of India** and served as the **Chief Minister of Bhopal**.
